items.title: GOP Now Stands for “Gang of Predators”
items.author: Lisa Graves
items.content:
It is both shocking and totally on brand for Donald Trump and JD Vance to defend Vivek Ramaswamy’s vile, million-dollar ad campaign weaponizing a child molester’s wife to attack Dr. Amy Acton, his opponent in Ohio’s gubernatorial race.

He continued to sexually abuse her until he was arrested when she was 12. The state took Amy and her little brother, Phil Stearns, away from Donna and Cledith. Phil stands by his sister, noting that Donna “stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died” in 2004.

Back in 1974, the year before he married Donna, Cledith Arthur had been charged with “incest” of a different child. That charge was two years before he began raping Amy.

That’s not all that is relevant and totally appalling.

In 1996, Donna Arthur–going by the last name “Hollopeter”--was found guilty of felony theft and passing bad checks. That is, the woman who Ramaswamy has lifted up to call her daughter a “liar” was literally convicted of the crime of “theft by deception,” which is stealing by lying. Donna–who lost custody of her children for neglect and for not protecting her daughter from a sexual predator–was also convicted of animal neglect, too, just five years ago in 2021.

You cannot make up such wretchedness.

In any sane universe, a candidate for governor would never run an ad featuring a child molester’s lover, a woman complicit in his abuse and also his after-the-fact accomplice.

Vivek’s action in taking her side is utter depravity.

Sure, Cledith Arthur pleaded “not guilty” before jumping bond and fleeing Ohio for Pennsylvania with his wife. Their flight from justice prevented a trial and his conviction as a monstrous pedophile, but I consider his evasion to be more evidence of his guilt.

And I will not call that woman Amy’s “mother” or “mom.” In my opinion, she forfeited that title when she betrayed her young daughter instead of protecting her from the predator she had invited into their lives. Now she has wormed her way out of the shadows to harm Amy, again, this time with the help of Vivek and his enormous wealth. There is a special place in hell for such betrayers of their sacred parental duty, like Alice Munro.

In any normal timeline, a candidate’s top advisors would resign if their boss insisted on running an attack ad siding with a child molester and his lover against the child who survived such horrifying abuse. Instead, Vivek’s spokesperson, Connie Luck, defended the ad and again attacked Dr. Acton’s character. That’s shameless, and I have a right to wish that Luck never has the good luck to get a good job ever again.

In any healthy administration, the president and the vice president would condemn the ad, urge Ramaswamy to take it down, and call on him to step down from the race.

But this is not a healthy administration. It is deeply unwell. It is morally sick.

I say this all in my personal capacity, not on behalf of any organization. Trump is wicked, a magnet of corruption, who attracts and collects the iron filings of men and women willing to trade their integrity for power, wealth, and fame—people like JD Vance.

Vance should have been unwelcome back in Ohio after telling foul lies about innocent, hard-working Haitian immigrants living in the state in 2024. After his defense of Vivek’s ad, Vance should be disowned by the state.

Despite his own track record, Vance—a recent Catholic convert—had the audacity this summer to try to lecture the Pope on Catholic tenets after Pope Leo rebuked the warmongering of Trump and Vance. Vance even published a memoir this year telling his tales about “finding my way back to faith,” a faith that includes the Ten Commandments, which expressly condemns bearing false witness. This week, rather than denounce Vivek’s ad featuring the child molester’s paramour, Vance assailed Acton’s character and dismissed any Republican critics, telling them to “stop whining.”

Vance should be ashamed. Instead, he is doubling down.

This would all be bad enough… but there’s more.

The Republicans installed a man who continues to act like Donald Trump’s personal defense attorney as Attorney General of the United States. That man, Todd Blanche, has expressed more sympathy for convicted sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell than for the victims and survivors of her schemes with Jeffrey Epstein. To this day, under Blanche’s direction, numerous Epstein-related records mentioning Donald Trump remain hidden. On Blanche’s watch, Maxwell was moved to a country club prison camp with more lenient conditions, and DOJ is investigating none of the other men named in the Epstein files.

His Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, was accused of raping a woman, who said she suspected he roofied her. Hegseth denied the claim before ultimately settling the case.

Trump’s Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh also faced an accusation of sexual assault from his former classmate, Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. He bombastically denied it and was confirmed to the nation’s highest court with Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) casting a pivotal vote in his favor, alongside nearly every other Republican senator.

Kavanaugh joined a Supreme Court where Republicans had previously installed Clarence Thomas, who was accused of repeatedly sexually harassing a woman who had worked for him. Thomas loudly denied the allegations too, but I found Anita Hill’s testimony compelling, just like Ford’s.

And this is only a partial accounting of the rot involving GOP men accused of sexual predators. Then there are the high profile men, like Ramaswamy and Vance, actively men credibly accused of rape, including the rape of children, as with Amy Acton’s case.

As I have said repeatedly since 2018, when Trump and his loyalist Republicans jammed Kavanaugh onto the Supreme Court (though he should have been impeached from the judiciary instead), America does not face a crisis of false accusations by women and girls. Most cases of rape are never reported. The real problem is false denials.

We have an epidemic of false denials.

That is partly because men accused of rape lie and deny that they did anything wrong.

And, in America, those who are accused have the right to plead not guilty, whether they are guilty or not, and face a trial with their neighbors as jurors. While most of those charges for sexual assault result in convictions or guilty pleas, we do not make an accounting of just how many of those men made false denials from the outset. Rarely do such trials result in acquittals or hung juries, but it sometimes happens after the defense tries to put the accuser on trial, scrutinizing what they wore, what they drank, or how they behaved.

Rarer still are the cases in which a man accused of molesting a child becomes a fugitive from justice, like the predator Donna Arthur repeatedly chose over her only daughter.

I hope justice prevails and the guy fueling these attacks–who I am going to call “Vivek Reallyslimy” from here on out–loses big time.

People of integrity and good conscience must take a stand against the dirtiest of dirty politics that he, Trump, and Vance are playing here.

I really hope a giant wave of justice breaks through and politically wipes out those who defend rapists and pedophiles and their enablers. And, I hope that wave also washes out any candidate for any office anywhere who refuses to condemn Reallyslimy’s ad and does not call on him to step down from the race.

The rest of us have had enough of this wickedness.

The time for accountability is well past due.

    • This book was written by two heroes of mine shortly after Thomas was installed on the Supreme Court. Jane and Jill are such excellent investigative reporters and writers. I look forward to their newest works.

items.title: Four of the Sitting Supreme Court Justices Helped George W. Bush Steal the Presidency Back in 2000
items.author: Lisa Graves
items.content:
On Tuesday, October 20, COURIER is hosting a must-watch event in partnership with Americans United: "Weaponizing Faith: Christian Nationalism at the Supreme Court."

I'm thrilled to moderate what I'm sure will be an illuminating, infuriating, and inspiring conversation about the forces behind the weaponization of the Roberts Court and key federal agencies, like the Pentagon under Pete Hegseth. Our panelists—Rachel Lazer, Mike Podhorzer, and Stasha Rhodes—have deep expertise in exposing and countering these extremists.

All Americans have the freedom to worship or not, but no American has the right to impose their religious agenda on the rest of us through the force of law. Regressive billionaires are fueling efforts to control who we can be, who we can love, and how we care for our bodies and families. Together, we can and must take a stand.

is a new podcast from the ACLU of Northern California examining urgent legal and social issues, from immigration to mass surveillance to voting rights—what’s at stake, why the ACLU gets involved, and whose rights are on the line. Listen now and learn more at aclunorcal.org.

Four of the Sitting Supreme Court Justices Helped George W. Bush Steal the Presidency Back in 2000

Four of the justices sitting on the U.S. Supreme Court today helped George W. Bush steal the presidency back in 2000 by helping stop the recount of Americans’ votes in Florida. Chief Justice John Roberts and Justices Brett Kavanaugh, Amy Coney Barrett, and Clarence Thomas each played different roles in the effort to use the Court to make Bush the 43rd president.

Fast forward to the summer of 2024. Those four were joined by two other Republican appointees–Sam Alito and Neil Gorsuch–in concocting presidential immunity from criminal prosecution for Donald Trump’s so-called “official acts,” paving the way for his return to power.

Why would any prudent person believe we can trust these five men and one woman to fairly rule on the coming onslaught of Trump’s efforts to subvert the counting of votes in November?

We must prepare to publicly, loudly, and relentlessly rebuke the Roberts Court if these partisans in black robes go along with Trump’s seizure of voting machines or efforts to stop the certification of our votes. Trump is desperate to prevent a Democratic majority in the House or Senate–one that could and would investigate the shocking corruption and destruction going on.

This rot affects us all. As James Talarico told Texans: “We have an affordability crisis because we have a corruption crisis.” We are suffering the consequences of Trump’s team selling us out, on top of his profoundly stupid tariffs and his reckless war, which are driving up the cost of living.

But the corruption does not stop there.

The Roberts Court corrupted our political system in the case by unleashing selfish billionaires to buy up politicians willing to slash their taxes–which were too low already–and deregulate or not regulate at all the industries that fuel their extreme wealth.

Clarence Thomas cast the tie-breaking vote in that case, which rewrote the Constitution to block Congress from enforcing laws like McCain-Feingold that regulated advocacy group spending near elections. He did so just weeks after his wife Ginni collected $500,000 from his billionaire benefactor Harlan Crow to fund her new Tea Party group that was positioned to take advantage of the ruling to come. In his concurrence, Thomas even had the audacity to claim that disclosing such funding would unconstitutionally chill the freedom of speech, including, apparently, the big secret gift Crow had just given his wife.

It is true that the Roberts Court has blocked a few–precious few–of Trump’s demands over the past 20 months. It blocked two Trump edicts that defied the plain language of the Constitution: one on congressional power over trade and another on the rights of Americans born here.

But those are exceptions.

Earlier this year, John Roberts wielded the judicial power with his five accomplices to destroy vital protections in the Voting Rights Act. That ruling, in the case, unleashed Republican legislatures to redraw election maps in ways that demonstrably diluted the votes of Black Americans. That resulted in white-dominated legislatures in what is technically the former Confederate States of America bleaching out Black representation in what recently dubbed a terrible, judicially-enabled return to the days of “Whites Only.”

Roberts and his clique insist that the Constitution hamstrings Congress when it suits them, yet it has repeatedly overturned lower court orders restraining Trump’s extraordinary claims of power for the Executive Branch—despite how he has transgressed the Constitution, statutes, regulations, and precedents and in spite of lower court findings of harm. That ongoing contradiction is astonishing. It is also unacceptable.

People ask me repeatedly: But why, why is the Court doing this?

The Republican majority on the Court was hand-picked not because they were believed to be fair but because they were thought to be loyal to the right-wing political agenda. And they are. Even though they have stopped a few of Trump’s more recent demands–for 2026, not for 2028, the next presidential election year–they have more cases coming their way involving voting, counting votes, certifying votes, and seating those elect.

We must not forget that John Roberts auditioned for his judicial appointment by helping George W. Bush stop the recount of American votes in the winter of 2000.

Roberts aided Bush’s brother Jeb, Florida’s governor at the time, in efforts to stop–or not stop–the certification of the state’s electoral college votes. He also helped his friend Michael Carvin prepare to argue against the recount. Carvin’s arguments failed before the Florida Supreme Court but were taken up by five Republican appointees to the U.S. Supreme Court in .

Just a few months later, Roberts was rewarded with a nomination to the D.C. Circuit and, a few years after that, with a nomination to the nation’s highest court. I detail this trajectory–and how Federalist Society leader Leonard Leo helped too–in my book Without Precedent: How Chief Justice Roberts and His Accomplices Destroyed the Constitution and Dismantled Our Rights.

Roberts was not alone among future Supreme Court justices in rushing to Bush’s aid. Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett volunteered to help, too.

Kavanaugh worked directly on Bush’s legal team, developing arguments for stopping the recount before the Florida Supreme Court. Unlike Roberts’ more secretive role, Kavanaugh was tapped to peddle those claims to the press, asserting what he called “the arbitrary, standardless nature of the recount process in Florida,” despite the standards election workers were following.

Kavanaugh was rewarded with a post in the White House Counsel’s Office, where he helped get Roberts on the D.C. Circuit. He later received his own judicial nomination.

Barrett (then Amy Coney) was on the scene early, too. She also headed to Florida at the outset of the litigation to help with research and briefs for Bush’s efforts to stop the recount.

In 2017, Leonard Leo worked with Trump’s White House Counsel to maneuver her onto the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and then on to the Supreme Court in late 2020.

Ginni was rewarded with a promotion at the Heritage Foundation and a raise, becoming its highest-paid employee who was not an executive on the board. Her new job was “Director of Executive Branch Relations” where she liaised with who at the White House? Kavanaugh.

Emails released in 2018 during Kavanaugh’s Supreme Court nomination show Ginni congratulating him on Republicans winning the Senate in the 2002 midterms. That electoral victory made it possible for the Republicans to get Roberts confirmed to the D.C. Circuit in May.

A few months later, in July 2003, Bush nominated Kavanaugh to the D.C Circuit.

What about Alito and Gorsuch? As a sitting judge, Alito could not join his fellow travelers, like former DOJ colleague John Roberts, in Florida to aid in .

But we all know what flag he flies.

After January 6, 2021, an upside-down American flag—a symbol tied to the violent assault on the Capitol unleashed by Trump—flew over Alito’s home until at least January 17. He blamed his wife, Martha, when the story broke a few years later, but the timeline shows this wasn’t a one-day fluke. A few years later, another flag tied to January 6, the Banner of Heaven flag, flew over Alito’s summer home. Again, he blamed his wife’s fondness for flags, yet he had no problem ripping down the rights of American women all across America in overturning .

As for Gorsuch, there are no news reports indicating that he joined the Florida crew. But he did eagerly join Roberts in rewriting the Constitution to invent criminal immunity for Trump and has sided with Roberts in recent cases aiding Trump’s electoral agenda.

As I describe in my book, when I was a career Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Office of Legal Policy at the Justice Department in 2001, I had to work with Ted Cruz, who had been rewarded for helping Bush with a job down the hall. In his office overlooking Constitution Avenue, I noticed a glass object that sparkled in the sun.

It was a paperweight with the words “Bush-Cheney Florida Recount Team 2000.”

The things sparkling in the sun were “chads,” the little pieces of paper that were part of the paper-punch ballots Republicans sought to block in the recount. With the recounts taking place in Democratic-majority counties and so few votes separating Bush from Al Gore, they argued that if a voter had not punched through the hole next to their preferred candidate’s name hard enough to release the chad, the vote should not count.

It was only through the partisan intervention of the Supreme Court that Bush became president; later tallies showed that Gore would have won Florida’s electoral votes.

I almost threw that paperweight out the window. Instead, I left my job at DOJ.

I wonder if Roberts, Kavanaugh, and Coney Barrett got that souvenir, too.
